Hi Sara —

Thanks again for taking time to walk through the deployment options yesterday. Attached is a consolidated redline to the Data Processing Annex that maps the key differences between Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) that we discussed:

- Private/on-prem: No outbound transfers by default; processing is explicitly constrained to customer-controlled network. Access for support/maintenance requires prior approval and can be limited to redacted telemetry.
- Dedicated: Data remains in customer-dedicated tenancy but some support telemetry and aggregated analytics may flow to Redwood for quality improvements; we propose contractual protections (pseudonymization + contractual limited purpose).
- Subprocessors: included updated matrix (attached). We added a 30-day notification window for new subprocessors and SCCs where applicable.

Can you confirm that this approach covers MediFin’s data residency requirements? If the wording looks good I can route the redline for signature via DocuSign. Attachment: Redwood_DPA_v3_processor_annex_redline.docx, subprocessor_matrix_20270420.pdf

High-level ask: please confirm whether MediFin needs a stricter prohibition on any outbound telemetry from Dedicated (i.e., zero-telemetry) or whether the pseudonymization + restricted use language suffices.

Thanks — happy to hop on another call if helpful.

—Marcus
Senior Sales Lead

Hi Marcus —

Appreciate the updates and the clear split. A couple of follow-ups from our security/privacy team:

1) Telemetry/analytics: For Dedicated we need to understand exactly what "aggregated analytics" includes. Does this cover error traces that include partial PII? If so we need either a strict no-PII guarantee or mandatory pseudonymization prior to any export.
2) Support access: We need a tightened operational carve-out. Specifically, support access should require a separate access ticket and be limited to session-level metadata unless explicit, documented escalation is approved by our security lead.
3) Cross-border transfers: For Private/on-prem you state "no outbound transfers by default" — we need that expressed as an explicit contractual prohibition unless there is a written, signed exception listing the specific data types and destination jurisdictions.

Can you ask legal to propose language for points 1–3? We can accept a 30-day notification for subprocessors but expect a 15-business-day review window for any changes affecting telemetry or egress.

Kevin — looping you in for legal redlines.

Thanks,
Sara
VP Product & Security
MediFin

Marcus —

Draft language below that I think balances MediFin's ask with operational needs. Pick the variant you want to propose: simple strict option, or a pragmatic option with pseudonymization.

1) Strict prohibition (customer-preferred):
"For Private/on-prem deployments, Redwood shall not initiate any transfer of Customer Data outside the physical boundaries designated in Exhibit A. Any transfer or export of Customer Data from a Private/on-prem deployment requires a Customer-signed exception specifying the data categories and destination jurisdictions."

2) Pragmatic (pseudonymization + restricted use):
"For Dedicated deployments, Redwood may process aggregated telemetry and operational metrics for service improvement provided that any telemetry that could reasonably identify an individual is pseudonymized and aggregated prior to export. Redwood shall not export raw user content or any data elements designated as PII in Exhibit B. Telemetry exports shall be limited to the minimum necessary for diagnostics and product improvement and shall be used only for the purposes set forth in Section X."

3) Support access (applies to both modes):
"Redwood support personnel may be granted time-limited access to Customer environments solely for troubleshooting pursuant to a documented access request. Access requires Customer approval and is limited to the minimum data elements necessary to resolve the incident. Elevated access actions will be logged and the logs made available to Customer upon request."

Other items: change notification window for subprocessor additions to 30 days is acceptable; MediFin's requested 15 business days for telemetry/egress-impacting changes is reasonable — propose a middle ground of 20 business days. Also recommend adding SCC reference and option for Customer to request subprocessor security evidence via the shared Drive link.

If that looks good I can format these as redline snippets and we can send back to Sara + Kevin.

-Laura
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
